correctness.rationale: For any loopless D with source s and sink t, top multipaths have exactly n-1 arcs. The closed star of b=t->s is a cone, the d-dimensional relative chains for d=n-2 are based on b-free Hamiltonian s-to-t paths, and deleting any arc makes each path compatible with b, so relative top differential is zero. Each such path closes to a forbidden directed Hamiltonian cycle whose boundary is an integral absolute top cycle with one unique non-star facet; these map onto the entire relative basis, proving the exact integral group. Collapsing the (d-1)-skeleton yields an explicit map that is degree one on the corresponding cycle boundary spheres, proving the homotopy retract. A standalone finite checker passed exhaustive n=3..5 digraphs and two parameter families with signed cycle checks.

originality.rationale: The 2022 primary paper computes the Euler characteristic of the one-arc-reversed transitive tournament but does not derive its top integral homology; its homotopy theorem applies to the unreversed transitive graph. Full source–sink feedback top cycles and splitting are neither stated nor implied by the inspected foundational results. The corresponding acyclic-digraph comparison cannot cover the directed cycles formed by the feedback edge. Multiple current published-result and primary-literature searches revealed no coverage; unindexed equivalent results remain a specific risk.

value.rationale: The result supplies a motivated all-digraph structural identification of top multipath homology with Hamiltonian source–sink path enumeration, not just ranks for a finite graph or an Euler characteristic. Canonical integral basis cycles and an explicit sphere-wedge homotopy retract convey more information than homology ranks. A bidirected internal-clique family yields factorially many top spheres for arbitrarily large n, and the reversed transitive tournament improves the particular earlier Euler-only example. Lower homology/full type are not claimed.
